skill.name: check-my-vibe
skill.description: Use when a user wants to review the public security posture of an AI-generated, vibe-coded, or deployed website through an authorized passive scan, especially for security headers, exposed secrets, source maps, public files, and deployment mistakes.
skill.summary: Guide an authorized passive website scan and turn supported findings into prioritized security fixes.
skill.author: daanaagua

security_audit.summary: The Markdown backticks are inline URL formatting, not shell execution, and the reconnaissance phrases describe scan limits and credential protections. The skill intentionally opens an external HTTPS scanning service and submits a public target URL, creating a limited third-party disclosure risk.

remediation.issue: Target URLs are submitted to an external scanning service.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users that the service receives the target URL, and advise them to remove sensitive query parameters before submission.

content.value_statement: Public websites can expose weak headers, secrets, source maps, and deployment mistakes. This skill guides an authorized Check My Vibe scan and converts evidence into prioritized fixes.
actual_capabilities: Confirms that the user owns the target or has permission before scanning.
Guides the user through a passive scan on the Check My Vibe website.
Reads completed scan scores, coverage states, findings, evidence, limits, and errors.
Separates urgent fixes from lower-priority and manual-review items.
Reports only vulnerabilities supported by scan evidence.
Explains verification failures, rate limits, invalid targets, and safely unreachable pages.
limitations: Requires a browser or a report pasted by the user.
Requires the user to complete Turnstile without automated assistance.
Does not test authenticated areas, private repositories, database authorization, or business logic.
A clean passive scan does not prove that a website is secure.

use_cases.title: Review a new deployment
use_cases.description: Check a newly published website for public configuration mistakes before wider release.

use_cases.title: Prioritize client fixes
use_cases.description: Turn supported scan evidence into an ordered remediation list for a client website.

use_cases.title: Validate release hygiene
use_cases.description: Review security headers, exposed files, and deployment signals during an authorized release check.

prompt_templates.title: Scan an authorized website
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Check My Vibe to review [URL]. I own this website or have the owner's permission. Summarize the supported findings and next steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan of one authorized public website

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a pasted report
prompt_templates.prompt: I cannot open the scanner here. Analyze this Check My Vibe report for [URL], separate findings by priority, and state all coverage limits: [REPORT].
prompt_templates.scenario: Review when browser access is unavailable

prompt_templates.title: Create a remediation plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the authorized scan for [URL]. Order fixes by severity, dependencies, and expected impact. Distinguish confirmed evidence from manual-review items.

prompt_templates.title: Perform evidence-focused triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the completed authorized scan for [URL]. Challenge weak evidence, identify partial coverage, group related findings, and provide the three highest-value actions with rationale.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced security triage with evidence quality checks

output_examples.input: Review my authorized production site and prioritize the scan results.
output_examples.output: Summary: The scan completed with partial coverage. Fix now: remove the exposed source map and strengthen the content security policy. Fix next: add missing browser security headers. Manual review: verify authenticated routes separately. Top actions: remove the source map, deploy the policy update, then repeat the scan.

output_examples.input: The scanner could not verify my site because it was rate limited.
output_examples.output: The scan did not produce verified findings because the target returned a rate-limit response. Use the service's normal retry path later. Do not change identity or bypass the limit. No security conclusion can be made from this attempt.

output_examples.input: Does a clean report mean my website is secure?
output_examples.output: No. A clean report only means this passive public-surface scan found no supported issues within its coverage. It does not validate authenticated access, database authorization, business logic, private code, or complete dependency risk.

best_practices: Confirm ownership or explicit permission before starting every scan.
Remove sensitive query parameters before submitting a target URL to the external service.
Preserve evidence, partial states, and coverage limits when prioritizing remediation.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a public URL as authorization to scan.
Do not invent vulnerabilities, code locations, scores, or scan results.
Do not bypass Turnstile, rate limits, same-origin checks, or URL safety controls.

faq.question: What does this skill scan?
faq.answer: It guides a passive review of one authorized public website through the Check My Vibe service.

faq.question: Do I need permission?
faq.answer: Yes. You must own the target or have the owner's permission before scanning.

faq.question: Can the skill complete Turnstile?
faq.answer: No. The user must complete Turnstile without automated bypass or assistance.

faq.question: What happens without browser access?
faq.answer: The skill provides the service URL and asks you to paste the completed report for analysis.

faq.question: Does the scan test authenticated features?
faq.answer: No. It does not log in or validate authenticated areas, database authorization, or business logic.

faq.question: Does a clean result prove the site is secure?
faq.answer: No. It only reflects supported findings within the passive scan's limited public coverage.
